Description : Hello, this issue is happening with certainty for cgilbert in WEB and mwooten in BEL, though I have received multiple reports from other locations as well, so I believe this to be universal. Scenario: Our bracer (DME specialist) needs to create a Provider Note with template type Knee Brace Order Form when ordering a brace. This is the Standard Written Order (SWO) that the APP (screening/re-eval provider) needs to sign in order to finalize the ordering of a brace. Title : Analytics Export Does Not Parse Double Quotes Appropriately

Issue : Bugs/Glitches

Description : Please see attached. The Double Quote character (") is not handled appropriately when exporting reports. This issue comes mostly from running an Admin Report for a large amount of appointments, opening in Excel, and having the data be misaligned. Sometimes there will be a Double Quote (") in the Comment field on an Appointment record. This issue can be exacerbated if commas are also included in the Comment, but all of it should be resolved by following the RFC-4180 standard. Prior to writing the data string to the file for export, replace all Double Quote characters (") with two Double Quotes (""). Note: If you export a report to CSV and then manually insert a (") after all of the (") characters that are desired as a part of the data (and not the ones meant to denote the start of the next cells data), then open the file in Excel; it works perfectly! Title : Selecting 2 or 3 Inj # Cuts PRP Narrative in Two

Location : Remote

Issue : Provider Note

Description : Hello. This may potentially be a larger issue than just with this one Custom Form, but I have not yet specifically seen it. There just isn't anything within this particular record that causes me to believe it is unique. More broadly, the narrative section of any given selection within a Custom Form may be cut off by the next narrative section, then continued afterwards; however, I will demonstrate this concern with the "PRP Injection Procedure" Custom Form record. Please see attached image for a visual representation. I can also provide a video if desired. If you create a Provider Note with template type "INJ- PRP Injection" then open the Custom Form titled "PRP Injection Procedure" and select "1" under the "Injection #" heading before finally hitting Save, the narrative works perfectly well. The issue comes in when you then have a second PRP injection and need to update the Custom Form with that new selection of "2" since all of the other data gets pulled forward. When you create that second note and open PRP Injection Procedure, then switch from "1" to "2" the narrative gets split. This persists if you select "3" as well; however it is able to be resolved by switching to "2", switching back to "1", then finally switching back again to "2" (all of this applies to the "3" option as well). Since this workaround exists (unintuitive though it may be), and PRP isn't a massive volume of appointments, this isn't super high priority. However, if the general concern of splitting narratives based on Custom Form selections does happen to exist in other records, debugging with this specific scenario should help understand and resolve any other concerns. Thank you for looking into this one!

Title : DUPE 9872 - Analytics Export Does Not Parse Double Quotes Appropriately

Location : Remote

Issue : Bugs/Glitches

Description : Hello. This is a duplicate of ticket #9872. I hadn't received any additional information regarding the ticket closure (as usually occurs if closed without completion), and the issue still persists in TH (many tickets are closed without additional information if they were simply resolved). Please see attached. The Double Quote character (") is not handled appropriately when exporting reports. This issue comes mostly from running an Admin Report for a large amount of appointments, opening in Excel, and having the data be misaligned. Sometimes there will be a Double Quote (") in the Comment field on an Appointment record. This issue can be exacerbated if commas are also included in the Comment, but all of it should be resolved by following the RFC-4180 standard. Prior to writing the data string to the file for export, replace all Double Quote characters (") with two Double Quotes (""). Note: If you export a report to CSV and then manually insert a (") after all of the (") characters that are desired as a part of the data (and not the ones meant to denote the start of the next cells data), then open the file in Excel; it works perfectly! Thank you very much.

Title : Feature Request: Confirmation on Next for Contact during Kiosk Check-In

Location : Remote

Issue : Check-In App

Description : Hello. Please see attached for reference. While checking in a patient through the Kiosk, on the Emergency Contact page, the Next button is currently able to be clicked when information exists on the form. I am requesting the implementation of a confirmation box rather than moving forward in this scenario. We could instead disable the button and add some text indicating that you must either save the information or remove it. Either way works perfectly fine. The goal here is to avoid scenarios where the form is filled out, but information is not saved. Clicking Save creates a Contact record and resets the form, so this wouldn't impact patients that either don't want to add a contact or ones that properly fill out and save the form. It would only affect patients that do want to add a contact and have filled out the form, but didn't realize that they specifically needed to hit Save prior to clicking Next. Technically, we could also just remove the Save button and run that function when clicking Next if information exists, but the specifics of implementation is really neither here nor there. Thank you very much for looking into this!

Title : Information Only: Updating Custom Form Causes Updates to Note Template(s)

Location : Remote

Issue : Settings

Description : Hello. This is more so just information for Hassaan that we had discussed on a recent call. No action necessarily needs to be taken, but rather I am documenting a potential concern when updating Custom Forms *if* it affects the data that comes over from the Kiosk into the Provider Note. I will use a recent update to Custom Form named "Chief Complaint - Lumbar" to illustrate. Currently, whenever an update is required for a Custom Form, I will update the Custom Form (Settings > EHRSettings > Custom Forms > Templates and Questionnaire) itself then remove it from the Kiosk Settings (Settings > Practice > KIOSK Settings) and hit Save. After this, I then reload the Kiosk Settings page, add that Custom Form back in, set the appropriate parameters (such as Reason List), and hit Save again. Note: I do *not* update any relevant Note Templates (Settings > EHRSettings > Note Template > Provider Note) that have the Custom Form within it. In this case, "EVAL - Lumbar and Hip Screening" is the only Note Template that contains this Custom Form. The potential concern here is that the Note Template (that was *not* updated, at least manually) shows as if it was updated at the same time the Custom Form (that certainly was updated) was updated. This is potentially not only perfectly fine, but also a fantastic feature that allows us to not have to update Note Templates whenever a Custom Form is updated. We are currently seeing some concerns come in regarding what data is being transferred from the Kiosk to the Note in ALP. The above may or may not be the issue, but I'm going to move forward with also updating the relevant Note Templates whenever I update a Custom Form just to be sure in the future. Finally, my only other hypothesis for this issue is that updating a Custom Form "removes" (it doesn't actually remove the data, but seems that way as the names are the exact same but the IDs are different so there genuinely isn't any data on the new one from a previous visit) the data that was in that Custom Form already from a previous visit. The system may be handling this perfectly well, but we're seeing concerns being reported as it very much so looks like an issue with the system.
